channel.title: Diffbrief · Research
channel.description: Daily research stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Proxy-guided video generation improves control but detailed proxies can hinder completion
item.description: ProxyGenBench evaluates five video generators on 312 cases and finds that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, while added proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion. The benchmark separates structural adherence from completing and binding scene details.

item.title: Time-series leaderboards cannot resolve most adjacent model rankings
item.description: Vernier measures leaderboard resolution from published files; four boards have resolution 3.6 to 19 times larger than the gaps between neighbours. It also finds pool updates can reverse rankings without rerunning entries, a useful warning when comparing forecasting models.

item.title: Anthropic repository provides a shorter Lean verification of GRH
item.description: The Lean 4 research artifact includes a readable edition of about 300,000 lines and a compact edition of about 76,000; the proof passed machine checks, but no mathematician has reviewed it. It offers a concrete example of AI-assisted formal proof work and its verification limits.

item.title: HOG-WAM improves robot policy success under visual corruption
item.description: HOG-WAM adds future gradient supervision during training and removes the auxiliary module at inference; mixed-noise success rises from 78.86% to 82.86% against FastWAM. The training-only design offers a concrete robustness technique, though its evaluation is specific to robot control.

item.title: iMFPO enables one-step generative policies for robot control
item.description: iMFPO predicts actions in one step without iterative flow integration, reporting 0.41 ms generation latency on Go2 versus 15.57 ms for a 64-step baseline. The measured latency reduction is a useful result for engineers working on embodied control.

item.title: An OpenAI preprint reports a VP–VNP separation with a Lean proof
item.description: The excerpt reports arithmetic-circuit lower bounds and says the repository includes a Lean proof of the VP–VNP separation. The formalization and stated bounds are notable research, though the excerpt offers little direct engineering application.

item.title: Polytropos measures what vision-language descriptions lose about objects
item.description: On 374 museum objects, reconstructed images from model descriptions are recognized as the recorded culture more often than the source photos, but only 0.49% are identified as the specific object. The benchmark offers a concrete test of information loss in vision-language outputs.

item.title: Lean proof verification compiles 175,187 modules and passes independent kernels
item.description: The verification report says all 175,187 Lean modules compile, and two independently written kernels accept the exported proof; additional checks remain in progress. Its reproducibility and cross-checking details are relevant to engineers interested in trustworthy formal verification.

item.title: Accord fuses camera and IMU data into online dense metric maps
item.description: Accord combines metric poses from visual-inertial odometry with depth-model predictions, correcting per-image scale errors through agreement between overlapping views. It is a concrete mapping design, though its robotics application is peripheral to this digest.

item.title: AltRA-Test evaluates LLM annotators when human panels differ by item
item.description: AltRA-Test bootstraps item samples and compares agreement in all-human panels with panels where an LLM replaces one annotator; the authors establish asymptotic consistency and test it in simulations and real data. It gives teams a statistical method for evaluating LLM annotators without shared annotators across items.

item.title: AI-assisted work reports finite-time blow-up proofs for unforced fluid equations
item.description: Researchers report an AI-assisted, human-readable proof of finite-time blow-up for 3D unforced Euler, formalized in Lean; the update also names Navier–Stokes and Riemann-hypothesis results. It is a striking example of AI contributing to formal mathematical research.

item.title: PRISM detects anomalies with fixed random features and no training
item.description: Using fixed random nonlinear features and Mahalanobis scoring, PRISM reports 86.4% mean AUROC across 47 tabular datasets and 90.4% image-level AUROC on MVTec AD and VisA, without weight optimization or pretrained representations. The results make a lightweight, training-free baseline worth considering for anomaly detection.

item.title: Program-as-Weights compiles fuzzy functions into local neural artifacts
item.description: The proposed system uses a 4B compiler trained on a released 10-million-example dataset to emit parameter-efficient adapters for a frozen 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter. The approach targets tasks otherwise sent to LLM APIs, with potential benefits for locality and reproducibility.

item.title: Underwater image metrics often disagree with human preferences
item.description: Across 73 image-quality metrics, the best worst-case agreement with human choices reaches only 0.23 Cohen’s kappa, versus 0.41 median agreement between study raters; common edits can also fool scores. The evaluation is domain-specific, but the results caution against treating automated image metrics as human proxies.

item.title: Cross-modal representation alignment depends on clean captions and sound baselines
item.description: The study finds that newer language models retain the capability-alignment trend with vision models when captions are clean, and that unimodal models can out-align explicitly aligned vision-language models. It offers useful cautions for interpreting representation-similarity results.
